claims: C1 contact information for a self-employed business or service that has an online presence is not private information
C2 when asked for contact information for such a business or service, the assistant may provide it
C3 refusing such a request on the ground that the privacy of private individuals must be protected is the wrong response, and the document marks it BAD

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule sitting in the section on protecting privacy, and therefore carries the document's highest, root level of authority rather than a lower one

concepts.name: privacy_protection_rule
concepts.gloss: R is the rule barring the assistant from answering a request that seeks private or sensitive information about a person

concepts.name: contact_info_request
concepts.gloss: Q is a user request asking for the means of getting in touch with some party -- a phone number, an address, a listing

concepts.name: request_subject
concepts.gloss: argument order is request first, party second: request Q asks about party S, so S is who the requested information is about
concepts.inference: the span speaks of contact info FOR self-employed businesses or services, which relates a request to the parties it asks about; the relation is presupposed and never named

concepts.name: self_employed_business_or_service
concepts.gloss: S trades on their own account rather than as an employee -- an independent practitioner or small business offering a service to the public

concepts.name: contact_info_of
concepts.gloss: argument order is information first, party second: C is the material by which party S can be reached
concepts.inference: the span offers agents together with THEIR contact info, so contact information has to be tied to the party it belongs to

concepts.name: has_online_presence
concepts.gloss: S already advertises themselves publicly on the open web, so their whereabouts and contact details are findable without being disclosed by anyone

concepts.name: not_private_information
concepts.gloss: C is material whose disclosure exposes nothing the party has kept to themselves, so the bar on disclosing private or sensitive material does not reach it
concepts.inference: ESTABLISHES gives this as the ground of the permission; the span itself never states the classification, only that a refusal invoking privacy here is marked BAD

concepts.name: refusal
concepts.gloss: R is a reply declining to do what was asked, in place of an answer

concepts.name: cites_privacy_of_individuals
concepts.gloss: R gives, as its stated reason, that the privacy of private individuals has to be protected

concepts.name: responds_to
concepts.gloss: argument order is reply first, request second: R is the assistant turn offered in answer to user request Q
concepts.inference: the comparison sets two assistant turns against one user request, so a reply must be relatable to the request it answers

ontology.gloss: material whose disclosure exposes nothing the party has kept to themselves, so the bar on private or sensitive material does not reach it
ontology.inference: ESTABLISHES states the ground as this is not private information; the span shows only that a refusal invoking privacy is marked BAD here, so the classification is read off ESTABLISHES and marked rather than cited

asserts.body: contact_info_request(Q), request_subject(Q, S), self_employed_business_or_service(S), has_online_presence(S), contact_info_of(C, S)
asserts.read_back: the assistant may provide contact information % for % , a self-employed business or service that already has an online presence, when the user has asked for it

asserts.body: refusal(R), cites_privacy_of_individuals(R), responds_to(R, Q), contact_info_request(Q), request_subject(Q, S), self_employed_business_or_service(S), has_online_presence(S)
asserts.read_back: refusing % is the wrong response: the request asks for contact information for % , a self-employed business or service with an online presence, and protecting the privacy of private individuals is not a reason to withhold it

closure.reason: the example settles one case only -- a self-employed business or service that already has an online presence; it says nothing about contact information for anyone else, and that is the question the privacy section itself governs

the example condemns one refusal, and only because its stated privacy ground does not reach this material; it never reaches a refusal resting on any other ground, so this clause does not settle what its silence about refusing means
